sections.sectionName: Part A — Conceptual Foundations (Answer All Questions)
sections.instructions: Short descriptive questions testing foundational understanding. 4 Marks each.

questions.text: Explain how HMAC-SHA256 tokens verify request authenticity and prevent parameter tampering in RESTful webhook endpoints.
questions.rubric: Secret pre-shared key, hash computation over full raw request payload, and constant-time string comparison.

questions.text: Explain the difference between strong consistency and eventual consistency with a distributed database example.
questions.rubric: Contrast synchronous quorum read/writes vs background gossip anti-entropy synchronization.

questions.text: Define CAP Theorem and state why network partitions cannot be completely eliminated in distributed clusters.
questions.rubric: State Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance trade-off with network latency reality.

sections.sectionName: Part B — Analytical Reasoning & Technical Derivations
sections.instructions: Detailed analytical problems testing algorithmic design and derivations.

questions.text: Demonstrate how formal verification using TLA+ model checking identifies distributed race conditions in two-phase commit protocols.
questions.rubric: Specification of states, temporal logic invariants (Inv_NoTwoDecisions), and state-space exploration.

questions.text: Describe the Circuit Breaker pattern states (Closed, Open, Half-Open) and write a pseudo-code implementation handling timeout thresholds.
questions.rubric: State transition machine with failure rate tripping threshold, sleep window timer, and canary probe requests.

questions.text: Derive the mathematical formulation of Scaled Dot-Product Attention and explain why sqrt(d_k) scaling prevents vanishing softmax gradients.
questions.rubric: Derivation: Softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) V. Variance of dot products grows with dimension d_k without scaling.

sections.sectionName: Part C — Architectural Synthesis & Capstone System Design
sections.instructions: Comprehensive long-form system architecture and fault-tolerant design challenges.

questions.text: Architect an event-driven saga orchestration pipeline for an enterprise university fee settlement system that guarantees idempotency.
questions.rubric: Choreography vs orchestrator comparison, compensating rollback transactions, and outbox pattern with Kafka/RabbitMQ.

questions.text: Evaluate FlashAttention IO-awareness compared to standard attention when training 32k context-length language models on modern GPU SRAM.
questions.rubric: Critical evaluation of HBM vs SRAM bandwidth bottlenecks, tiling outer loops, and online softmax recomputation.

questions.rubric: Apply R + W > N and W > N/2. For N=9, R=5, W=5 or R=4, W=6 satisfies strict quorum intersection.

questions.text: Analyze the Raft consensus leader election protocol during split-vote scenarios and show how randomized election timeouts prevent livelock.
